terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent, with a question
evidence: Ter. Eun. 290: mīror quid ex Pīraeeō abierit
Caes. BG 1.32.2: ejus reī quae causa esset mīrātus
terms.comment: With a question it wonders with a touch of surprise: mīror quid hoc sit negōtī, I wonder what’s up (Traupman 111, 408). Plain curiosity is velim scīre. To wonder at something, or marvel, see be surprised.

terms.gloss: I’d like to know, I wonder (whether, what)
terms.grammar: with a question; num or -ne for “whether”
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.9.1: sānē velim scīre num cēnsum impediant tribūnī
terms.comment: The polite wondering of Cicero’s letters, where it is very frequent.

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent, with a question
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: mostly in the first person present, and peculiar to the language of conversation.

phrases.latin: Mīror quid ex Pīraeeō abierit; nam ibi custōs pūblicē est nunc.
phrases.english: I wonder why he has left the Piraeus; he is on guard duty there just now.

phrases.latin: et tamen velim scīre quid cōgitēs
phrases.english: and yet I wonder what you have in mind
I wonder where Messenio has wandered off to now.
